title: NATS KV values: bucket registry (keys <host>.<env>.nodes|workflows|models|loras|looks), bucket hosts (key <host>.<env>) and bucket host_settings (key <host>)
description: Each runner writes only its own keys: the registry keys at start (from API 1.16 `models` and `loras` again whenever a rescan finds a change: every 60 s and after each model job), its hosts key every 10 s (studio treats a hosts key older than 30 s as offline). studio_service reads them, and alone writes bucket host_settings (the admin's per-host settings, API 1.16), which the runners of that host watch. Every value carries schema_version (major, versioned like a message).

portType.description: a port's value type; an input accepts an output of the same type, and an input of type Media also accepts Image, Video and (API 1.30) Audio (contracts/README.md, Graph rules: fits). Text, Image, Video (an MP4, may carry audio), Audio (API 1.30: speech, a WAV {wav, sample_rate, duration_s}: PCM 16-bit, mono, the model's own rate), Int, Float, Seed, Canvas, Duration ({frames, fps}) are plain values; Media is an input type only (the output node's `media`), never an output or a param; Model, Conditioning, Latent are family-scoped handles: they only wire nodes of one family inside one workflow and never cross a process (Latent[ltx] carries the video and audio latents together)

optional.description: inputs only: true = may be left unwired (the feature is off; the stage gets no such key); absent = false, a required input

paramSchema.description: one param of a node; the UI derives a form field from it. int, float and seed: min/max bound the value, step is the field's increment; string and text (multi-line): min/max bound the length; enum: one of `enum`. seed: an int where null or -1 means random (the runner picks one and reports it in evt.run.status resolved.seed and each output's seed). image: one Image, written {take_id} by clients (default null = none; a run needs one). rows: an ordered list of items (default []), min/max bound the count, `item` names each item's fields, `mention` is how the prompt refers to item n (from 1). frames: a frame count on the family's frame grid, min + k × step (k ≥ 0) up to max (LTX: 9 + 8k, 9..321); `fps` names the node's fps param; the UI renders it as the Duration slider (one notch per step, labelled frames and seconds). frames may declare `auto` (the model predicts the length: the value "auto"). int may declare `values` (the only allowed values) and `values_by` (the allowed values per value of an enum param of the same node: LTX steps per role); from API 1.39 an enum may declare `values_by` too, and its `param` may name another node's enum param (`model.variant`: LTX extend's direction per model variant). From API 1.19: media: one video or audio take (`accepts`), written {take_id[, in, out]} by clients (default null; a run needs one); `trim`: it reads the part in..out (the UI's trim control over the take); `grid`: a video's sides must be multiples of it; `max_s`: the longest take (or part) it reads; `max_frames`: the most frames of a video take it reads. span: a time range {start, end} on the workflow's one video media source (default null; a run needs one; the UI's range control over that take). contracts/README.md, Media inputs. From API 1.30: voice: one saved voice (a library item of kind voice), written {voice_id} by clients (default null; a run needs one); `accepts` names the voice sources it takes: preset (a pack's starter voice of the node's family), clip (from API 1.31: a voice with a clip, cloned or designed; studio sends its clip as a media value), design (a voice from a description). It takes no wire; from API 1.32 it may be a rows item field (a dialogue's `lines`). contracts/README.md, Voices. From API 1.32: a `text` param may declare `script: true` (a dialogue script: studio expands it into the same node's `lines` rows at create time; contracts/README.md, Dialogue)

name.description: unique among the kind's params and inputs; `bypass` is reserved (the Studio path <node>.bypass)

fps.description: frames only: the name of the same node's int or float param that holds frames per second; the UI shows the length as frames / fps seconds

auto.description: frames only: present = the model can predict the clip's length from the prompt; the value "auto" asks for it. The prediction is clamped to min_s..max_s seconds and to the param's min..max frames, then put on the grid (contracts/README.md, Video: auto length). The UI draws the Duration slider's Auto length switch from it

label.description: the field label; absent = the name

step.description: int, float, seed: the field's increment (int: an integer)

values.description: int only: the only allowed values, ascending, each within min..max, the default among them; the UI draws a choice (one allowed value: a read-only readout), studio refuses others (`<node>.<param>: must be one of <values>`)

values_by.description: int with `values`, or (API 1.39) enum: the allowed values depend on the value of an enum param `param`: of the same node (`role`), or (API 1.39) of another node of the graph in the `when` reference form `<node id>.<param>` (`model.variant`, read from the graph's merged values; a graph without that node, or a value not listed, allows all). values[that value] is a subset of `values` (int) or `enum` (enum); an enum's default is in every subset of a cross-node values_by, so a node placed with its defaults never breaks it. The message names that subset (LTX sample: role stage1 -> [8], stage2 -> [3]; LTX extend: model.variant distilled -> [after], `extend.direction: must be one of after`)

note.description: from API 1.40, a cross-node values_by only: the line the UI shows under the choice of `param` while this refuses one of its options (LTX extend: `Dev: the only model that extends before. About 10× slower.`, board LtxFeatures frame 8). Absent = each refusal (`Extend before needs Dev`)

when.description: visibility expression over the graph, e.g. "model.variant != 'turbo'" (<node id>.<param>); absent = always shown. Carried through as is; studio evaluates it in a later stage, the runner ignores it

item.description: rows only: field name → a ref kind (the field holds a value of that kind, required in every item: Image = an image take {take_id}; Media (API 1.14) = an image or a video take {take_id}, an ask node's `media`; Lora = a LoRA {lora_id}, contracts/README.md, LoRAs) or a param schema (without name; not rows); from API 1.22 that may be a `media` param (a video or audio take {take_id[, in, out]}, required in every item; from API 1.37 one with `optional` may be null)

mention.description: rows only: the text by which a prompt refers to item n (from 1), e.g. <image{n}>; the prompt carries it as is, the pack does not rewrite it

accepts.description: media only (required): the take kinds it takes. video: a video take (its picture and sound); audio: an audio take, or a video take's sound (one without sound is refused). From API 1.30, voice only (required): the voice sources it takes, 1-3 of preset, clip, design

trim.description: media only: true = the value may carry in/out (the part read; the UI draws a trim control on the take); absent/false = the whole take, in/out refused

grid.description: media only: a video take's width and height must be multiples of it (LTX: 32)

max_s.description: media only: the longest it reads, in seconds: a whole take's duration, or out - in with trim

max_frames.description: media only (API 1.19): the most frames of a video take it reads (its `frames`, at any fps; LTX: 321)

not_with.description: rows only (API 1.22): optional inputs of the same node; while any of them is wired the rows must stay empty (studio 422 `<node>.<param>: must stay empty while <node>.<input> is wired`), mentions add no rows to it and "Use in…" does not count it (MiniMax H3: references cannot go with a first or last frame). contracts/README.md, Media inputs: rows of media

addons.description: enum only (API 1.41, contracts/README.md "Optional add-ons"): value → the optional add-ons (components of the node family's models entry `addons`) a run needs while the param holds that value (MiniMax H3's `lora`: `turbo` → [turbo]); each key one of `enum`. The run check counts them as the node's own `addons` (Several hosts: eligibility, step 2b), on the node's resolved value, never while the node is bypassed. Absent = no value needs one

addons_with.description: enum with `addons` only (API 1.41): `<name>` → {value → add-ons}, `<name>` an optional input of the same node or one of its rows params, and the values those of `addons`. While that input is wired, or that rows param holds a row, its list replaces the value's `addons` list (several such names: their lists together): MiniMax H3's generate runs Ref2VA with any reference, so `lora: turbo` then needs `turbo_ref` instead of `turbo`

max_total_s.description: rows only (API 1.22), with exactly one media field in `item`: the most seconds its items read together (each item's out - in, or the whole take without trim); over it is 422 `<node>.<param>: the takes last <d> s in all; at most <max_total_s> s`

min_s.description: media only (API 1.22): the shortest it reads, in seconds: a take shorter is refused (`take <id> lasts <d> s; this input takes at least <min_s> s`), and with trim so is a shorter part (`the part lasts <d> s; …`)

script.description: text only (API 1.32): the param is a dialogue script. Studio expands it at create time into the node's rows param `lines` (item fields voice, text, style, pause_s), each non-empty line `@handle: text` or `@handle (style): text` speaking in that element's voice; the run gets the script empty. Not scanned for ordinary mentions; it takes no wire (contracts/README.md, Dialogue)

rules.description: from API 1.47 (contracts/README.md, Param rules): refusals as data (model.yaml `rules`). While `when` holds (the `when` grammar plus <, <=, >, >=, + - * /, len(<rows>) and gcd(a, b); a bare name is a param of the same node, or in a rows item field's rule a field of the same item; <a>.<b> is param b of the node wired into input a, else of node a) the run is refused `<node>: <error>` (an item field's `<node>.<param>[<i>].<field>: <error>`), `{<expression>}` in error replaced by its value; a reference that resolves to nothing makes the rule not hold. Studio checks them (422), the form shows them under the param; the runner ignores them

option_help.description: from API 1.47, enum or int with values: value (as text) -> its line under the value in the param's menu (model.yaml `option_help`)

itemParam.description: a rows item field that is a param: a paramSchema without name, not rows or image (an item may add `position`); from API 1.22 a `media` param (required in every item unless, from API 1.37, `optional`); from API 1.32 a `voice` param (a dialogue line's speaker: required in every item, never left out)

label.description: the field label; absent = the name

step.description: int, float, seed: the field's increment (int: an integer)

position.description: float only: the field is a time on the clip in seconds (a keyframe's place): studio turns it into the pixel frame min(round(s * fps), F - 1) of the workflow's frames param and refuses rows past the clip or on a frame another row uses (contracts/README.md, Video: keyframes); the rows editor draws it on the clip's length

accepts.description: media only (required): the take kinds it takes. video: a video take (its picture and sound); audio: an audio take, or a video take's sound (one without sound is refused). From API 1.32, voice only (required): the voice sources it takes, 1-3 of preset, clip, design

trim.description: media only: true = the value may carry in/out (the part read; the UI draws a trim control on the take); absent/false = the whole take, in/out refused

grid.description: media only: a video take's width and height must be multiples of it (LTX: 32)

max_s.description: media only: the longest it reads, in seconds: a whole take's duration, or out - in with trim

max_frames.description: media only (API 1.19): the most frames of a video take it reads (its `frames`, at any fps; LTX: 321)

min_s.description: media only (API 1.22): the shortest it reads, in seconds: a take shorter is refused (`take <id> lasts <d> s; this input takes at least <min_s> s`), and with trim so is a shorter part (`the part lasts <d> s; …`)

optional.description: media only (API 1.37): the field may be left empty (null or absent) in an item; its default is null. Absent = required in every item. A rows param's `max_total_s` and Use in… offers go by the item's one required media field (contracts/README.md, Media inputs: rows of media)

rules.description: from API 1.47 (contracts/README.md, Param rules): refusals as data (model.yaml `rules`). While `when` holds (the `when` grammar plus <, <=, >, >=, + - * /, len(<rows>) and gcd(a, b); a bare name is a param of the same node, or in a rows item field's rule a field of the same item; <a>.<b> is param b of the node wired into input a, else of node a) the run is refused `<node>: <error>` (an item field's `<node>.<param>[<i>].<field>: <error>`), `{<expression>}` in error replaced by its value; a reference that resolves to nothing makes the rule not hold. Studio checks them (422), the form shows them under the param; the runner ignores them

option_help.description: from API 1.47, enum or int with values: value (as text) -> its line under the value in the param's menu (model.yaml `option_help`)

family.description: the model family (the kind's prefix); null for a core node

component.description: from API 1.24: the model component the node loads, in words (model.yaml `stages.<name>.component`: transformer, text encoder, vae); the Graph inspector reads `<family> · runs on <runtime> · uses the <component>`. Absent = it loads none (core nodes, canvas, duration, the model and LoRA stack nodes)

addons.description: from API 1.36 (contracts/README.md, Optional add-ons): the optional add-ons the node loads, each a `component` of its family's models entry `addons` (model.yaml: a component with `addon` in the stage's `uses`). A run in which the node is not bypassed is eligible only on a host where each is present; the UI shows the node's controls greyed while it is not ("Enhancer not downloaded"). Absent = none

phases.description: from API 1.36: the ordered phases of a node that runs one engine end to end (model.yaml `stages.<name>.phases`; MiniMax H3's generate: encode, sample, decode_audio, decode_video), ids unique. Its evt.run.progress carries `phase_id`, one of these ids (contracts/README.md, Phases); the UI draws one chip per phase, the current one with its step n/N. Absent = none

peak_gb.description: from API 1.47: the stage's peak_gb formula (model.yaml), published only for a stage that uses no component (a native child process: its memory plan is the formula alone, contracts/README.md Memory per run); studio evaluates it per run. Absent = none

sounds.description: from API 1.47: the limits on the sound the node's references carry together (model.yaml `stages.<name>.sounds`; MiniMax H3: 15 s, 3 inputs): audio rows, and video rows whose sound is kept or replaced; the composer counts them

media.description: what its runs make: image / video / (API 1.30) audio takes (the Image / Video / Audio switch filters templates by it), or from API 1.14 `text`: an answer stored on the run, no take (an ask workflow: its `answer` node; contracts/README.md, The llm pack). Absent = image. Must equal what studio computes from the graph (contracts/README.md, Video: a workflow's media). A text workflow is internal: never listed for Create, never run from Create or a workflow batch; only a pipeline's judge, write and decide nodes run it

nodes.description: params here override the node schema's defaults; the run's inputs override both

studio.description: the Studio (Create) layout studio sends as the template's Workflow.studio; absent = the derived form. Its paths obey the graph rules for a user workflow's block (studio_unknown_path, studio_duplicate)

action.description: API 1.19: the take action's label when this workflow is offered for a take ("Use in…", a Timeline clip's actions): Animate, Edit, Extend, Retake a section; absent = the title

nodes.description: registry key <host>.<env>.nodes: every node kind this runner can execute

workflows.description: registry key <host>.<env>.workflows: the workflows this runner offers; each workflow's env is the key's env and uses only kinds in its .nodes

models.description: registry key <host>.<env>.models: the models present on this host for this env

variants.description: the model's variants on this host (section 9.2 of docs/plan/06-platform.md); absent for a model without variants (echo)

id.description: the value of the family's model node variant param

presence.description: present: every file of the variant (its own and the shared ones it loads) is on disk and no recorded hash differs; partial: some are (an interrupted or cancelled download: resume it); missing: none of its own; mismatch (API 1.16): a file's SHA-256 differs from the one recorded at download (`mismatch` names them; the variant does not load until it is downloaded again). partial and mismatch are from API 1.16; the dispatcher treats every value but present as not runnable

bytes.description: size on disk of the variant's own files (shared files counted once, in the variant that owns them); absent when missing

precisions.description: what it can load as, first = native. A full-precision variant lists its dtype then the load-time quantizations (bf16, int8; MLX also int4); an already-quantized one lists only its own (int8; from API 1.33 fp8: a community pre-quantized variant, model.yaml `variants.<id>.precision`): no choice, nothing quantized at load

memory.description: from API 1.13 (contracts/README.md, The hand-over): per precision of `precisions`, what a run of this variant loaded at that precision holds. The dispatcher's host admission reads it; a precision not listed is planned at the whole host budget. Native runners publish it for every present variant and precision

peak_gb.description: the planned peak: the most this env holds at once during such a run at the canonical workflow's default sizes, starting warm (every component without unloads_after resident): max over its stages of the resident components + the stage's own + the stage's peak_gb formula. LoRAs not included. Sizes are this host's: each runner plans for its own device (model.yaml may give per-device sizes), so one variant may plan differently on two hosts; on cuda, components on the device only (VRAM)

planned_at.description: from API 1.13: the largest sizes peak_gb was planned at, over its stages (the formulas' mp and frames). A run larger than either (any node's width × height / 10^6, any numeric frames) has no plan: it is planned at the whole host budget. Absent: every run uses peak_gb

images.description: from API 1.14, ask workflows: the most thumbnails (each image take 1, each video take 3 keyframes) peak_gb was planned at; a run sending more has no plan (planned at the whole budget). Absent: not a limit

components.description: every component such a run loads, in the order of their last use in the run (the hosts value's resident entries of the same key). From API 1.21 it may be empty: a native pack's stage runs a child process that loads its own weights and exits, so nothing stays resident and the plan is peak_gb alone

variant.description: the variant that owns the files (Qwen turbo's text_encoder and vae: base): the resident entry's variant

precision.description: what it is loaded at (a vae stays bf16 in an int8 run): the resident entry's precision

unloads_after.description: true: the run unloads it after its stage (a stage's unload_after), so it is not resident after the run; absent = false

device.description: from API 1.18, cuda hosts: held in host RAM (CPU offload): the resident entry's device; not in peak_gb, in ram_peak_gb

workflow.description: from API 1.14: this item plans only runs of that workflow (an ask workflow that loads one component of the family: `qwen-image-ask` loads the text encoder only). The dispatcher takes the item of the run's precision and workflow, else the item of its precision without `workflow`. Items are unique by (precision, workflow)

ram_peak_gb.description: from API 1.18, cuda hosts: the most host RAM such a run holds at once (the CPU-side components, one tensor's pinned staging per load, the runtime). The dispatcher fails a run whose ram_peak_gb exceeds the host's host_ram.budget_gb, as it does for peak_gb. Absent = not a limit

title.description: from API 1.16: the variant's display name (`Turbo`, `Distilled int8`); absent = the id

dir.description: from API 1.16: its folder under the host's models root (`Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo`): model.yaml `variants.<id>.dir`

source.description: from API 1.16: where a download fetches the variant's own files (model.yaml `variants.<id>.source`): huggingface_hub.snapshot_download(repo_id=repo, revision=revision, allow_patterns=allow_patterns, local_dir=<models root>/<dir>). Absent: the variant cannot be downloaded (put its files there by hand); from API 1.33 a variant may also fetch from `sources` into the same folder: `bytes` then counts them too, and `gated` is true when any of them is

components.description: from API 1.16: every weight component the variant loads, in model.yaml order

from_variant.description: the variant whose folder it loads from: itself, or the owner of a shared component (`shares`; Qwen turbo's text_encoder and vae: base)

precisions.description: what it can load at; with `stored`, one that differs from it is made at load (int8 from bf16), else first = as stored and the rest are load-time quantizations

stored.description: from API 1.34: the dtype most of its weight bytes have on disk, read from its safetensors headers (BF16, F16, F32, F8_E4M3 / F8_E5M2 = fp8, I8 = int8). Absent when its files are on no disk of this host or their format does not say (GGUF, packed U8 / U32)

bytes.description: on disk (its files in from_variant's folder); absent when missing

separate.description: true: a shared component kept as this variant's own copy on this host because its files' hashes differ from the owner's (from_variant is then the variant itself); absent = false

files.description: from API 1.16: the manifest of the variant's own folder: every file the runner found (or a download wrote), path relative to `dir`, sorted. Absent when missing, or left out while the models value would pass 768 KB (largest first)

sha256.description: recorded at download (the Hub's LFS hash, checked), or hashed once by the runner and kept by path, size and mtime; absent while not known yet

component.description: the component whose glob matches it; absent for configs

mismatch.description: from API 1.16, presence mismatch only: the files (relative to `dir`) whose SHA-256 on disk differs from the recorded one, sorted

sources.description: from API 1.33: more repos a download fetches after `source`, into the same folder (`dir`), in order (a community pre-quantized variant: configs from the official repo, weights from the community one). Each is planned as `source` is; a path two of them list fails the plan. The licence, must_accept and gated of the whole download are `source`'s. Absent: `source` alone

revision.description: a commit SHA (preferred: pinned), tag or branch

allow_patterns.description: fnmatch globs over that repo's paths

gated.description: the repo needs a Hub token: the runner reads it from the host's secrets file (RUNNER_HF_TOKEN_FILE); never in a message, the API or a log

bytes.description: the expected download size of this repo's files (counted again in the variant's `source.bytes`)

dir.description: from API 1.33: the folder under the models root its files land in, instead of the variant's `dir`: a component's own `dir` (model.yaml `components.<c>.dir`; MiniMax H3 Image's prompt enhancer, MiniMax-H3-Image-PE). Files already there at the Hub's hash are kept; a delete of the variant never removes them (every variant of the pack reads that folder)

devices.description: from API 1.33: the only devices the variant runs on (model.yaml `variants.<id>.devices`: a community FP8 or int8 variant is [cuda]). A runner on another device does not publish the variant at all, so the Models screen never offers it there and the dispatcher never sends it a run of it. Absent: every device of the model's runtimes

distill_from.description: M9: the variant whose weights are this one's distilled model, built in (model.yaml `variants.<id>.distill_from`: ltx dev-int8's is distilled-fp8, the dev transformer with the distilled LoRA fused in): `<family>/distill` on this variant loads that variant's transformer, no LoRA, so a host qualifies for it when that variant is present there. Absent: the distill bakes the family's pre-fused distilled LoRA (`lora.prefused`, variant distilled)

help.description: from API 1.39: the variant's line under its title in the model chip's menu (model.yaml `variants.<id>.help`; LTX's Distilled `8 steps, about 10× faster`)

lora.description: present when the family takes LoRAs on this runner's runtime (it publishes a <family>/lora-stack node; ltx: the mlx runner only, model.yaml `lora.runtime`)

media.description: from API 1.16: what the model makes (`[image]`, `[video, audio]`), from model.yaml `media`

runtime.description: torch, mlx, native (from API 1.21: a stage runs a child process, Apple silicon only), fake

devices.description: from API 1.18: the devices the runtime runs on (model.yaml `runtimes.<r>.devices`); absent = every device of that runtime (mlx, native: mps)

runtimes.description: from API 1.16: every runtime the pack has (model.yaml `runtimes`), also those of other envs: a model whose only runtimes are mlx or native runs only on Apple silicon

addons.description: from API 1.36 (contracts/README.md, Optional add-ons): the model's optional add-ons on this host, model.yaml order: components (`components.<c>.addon`) that some nodes load (their `addons`) and no variant needs. A variant is present without them, and never lists them in its components, files or bytes; each is downloaded and deleted on its own (cmd.model.job `addon`). Absent = none

title.description: its display name (`Enhancer`): the Models screen's, a job's and, without `short`, the run check's and the UI's `<title> not downloaded`

short.description: from API 1.40: the name the run check and the UI use in `<short> not downloaded` (model.yaml `addon.short`: Qwen Image's two enhancers are both `Enhancer`, as the controls see one). Absent = `title`

tag.description: from API 1.40: the Models screen's mono line beside the title (model.yaml `addon.tag`: `PE-T2I`). Absent = the component id

refs.description: from API 1.40 (contracts/README.md, Optional add-ons): the task whose runs need it (model.yaml `addon.refs`): true = only a run with references (an Image value in its graph: an edit, Qwen's PE-I2I), false = only one without (text to image, PE-T2I). Absent = both

help.description: what it adds, for the Models screen

dir.description: its folder under the models root: the component's own `dir`, else the first variant's (its files then never count as that variant's)

presence.description: as a variant's, over the add-on's own files only: present = its globs match and no download of it is unfinished and no recorded hash differs

bytes.description: its files on disk; absent when missing

source.description: where a download of the add-on fetches its files, into `dir` (model.yaml `components.<c>.addon.source`). Absent: not downloadable (put its files there by hand)

variants.description: from API 1.40 (contracts/README.md, Optional add-ons): the variants whose runs need it (model.yaml component `variants`: LTX's distilled LoRA is Dev's fast-distill stage, its detailer Distilled's detail pass); a run on another variant of the model does not need it. A runner lists an add-on only when it runs one of these. Absent = every variant

mismatch.description: presence mismatch only: its files (relative to `dir`) whose SHA-256 on disk differs from the recorded one, sorted

compute.description: from API 1.39 (contracts/README.md, Video: Audio relay, compute, negative prompts): present when the model node's `compute` holds on this runner's runtime (ltx: mlx; model.yaml `model.compute`): the components it applies to. A run whose `compute` is not float32 needs those entries at its compute (Order and Admission: Entry, Plan, Resident)

licences.description: from API 1.16: the full text of every licence a variant's `source.licence` names (from the pack's licences/<id>.md), each once; shown before a download

id.description: an SPDX id or the pack's own (`apache-2.0`, `ltx-2-community`)

url.description: where the licence is published, for reference

loras.description: registry key <host>.<env>.loras: the shared LoRAs this runner indexed on its host (every *.safetensors under <models>/loras/ and under any loras/ folder inside a model folder), written at start. Studio's LoRA library lists the union over live hosts; the dispatcher sends a run that names a shared LoRA only to a host whose key lists it

id.description: the file's SHA-256 (the runner hashes it once and keeps the hash by path, size and mtime): the LoRA's id everywhere

name.description: the file name without .safetensors, cut to 80

family.description: the first family of this runner's packs (by name) the normaliser fits it to (every key applied or ignored, at least one applied); unknown when none

licence.description: __metadata__ modelspec.license, else license, trimmed; null when neither

host.description: bucket hosts, key <host>.<env>: the runner's live state, rewritten every 10 s. Never shown to users as is: GET /v1/studio/hosts redacts it.

run_id.description: the run in progress (busy), else null

memory.description: the memory admission counts (contracts/README.md, The hand-over; Hosts with a discrete GPU). budget_gb = the device memory the runner may use: unified RAM minus the reserve on mps (as before), VRAM minus the reserve on cuda, RAM minus the reserve on cpu; the host's shared budget is the smallest budget_gb of its envs. used_gb = what the process holds there now: mps the process's phys_footprint; cuda torch.cuda.memory_reserved() + the CUDA context (device used just after the runner created its context, before any tensor, measured once at start); cpu the process's resident set

device.description: from API 1.18: the device the runner computes on (its torch device, or MLX's Metal = mps; native: its child's Metal = mps), picked once per process (mps, then cuda, then cpu)

name.description: torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) (`NVIDIA L4`); on Apple silicon the chip (`Apple M3 Max`); cpu: the CPU model or `cpu`

memory_total_gb.description: the device's memory: VRAM (cuda: torch.cuda.mem_get_info()[1]); unified RAM (mps); RAM (cpu)

memory_used_gb.description: cuda only: the whole device's used memory, every process (total - free of torch.cuda.mem_get_info()); shown to admins, never counted by admission

capability.description: cuda only: the compute capability (`8.9`); below 8.0 has no bf16, so a bf16 component loads as fp16

driver.description: cuda only: the NVIDIA driver version (`580.95.05`)

runtime.description: the compute stack (`torch 2.15.0 · CUDA 13.2`, `torch 2.15.0 · MPS`, `mlx 0.30.0`; native: the binary, `h3 4cafd17`)

host_ram.description: from API 1.18, only when the device has its own memory (cuda): the second limit, host RAM. budget_gb = machine RAM - RUNNER_RAM_RESERVE_GB (default 4); used_gb = the process's resident set (pinned staging and CPU-side components included). Absent on mps and cpu, where `memory` is that RAM

resident.description: model components loaded now (the residency manager's view)

model.description: a model id of the models key

compute.description: from API 1.39: the entry's load option `compute` (the model node's, for the components the models key's `compute.components` names); absent = float32, which the runner never sends. A float16 entry is its own entry, beside a float32 one of the same component

pinned.description: in use by the running run (never evictable), or pinned by the host's setting (RUNNER_PIN; from API 1.16 the host's pins): kept by idle and after-run unloads, a hand-over victim only as the last resort. In an idle runner's value only the setting's pins are true

last_used.description: from API 1.13: when a stage last used it (its load counts as a use); the dispatcher's victims go least recently used first. Native runners always send it; absent = used before any entry that has it

loras.description: a component with LoRAs baked in (mode bake) is its own entry: those LoRAs, in order; absent or empty = the plain component. Adapter LoRAs are not listed. GET /v1/studio/hosts shows another user's own LoRA only as its size

pinned_why.description: from API 1.16, with pinned true: in_use = the running run uses it; pin = the host's pins (bucket host_settings, else RUNNER_PIN) name it. A pin is a hand-over victim only as the last resort (after every unpinned one, when the run would not fit otherwise); an admin unload unloads it anyway; the pin stays set

device.description: from API 1.18, cuda hosts: the component is held in host RAM (CPU offload); it counts against host_ram, never against memory, and is never a hand-over victim. Absent = on the device

attempt.description: the attempt of run_id in progress (busy); absent when idle. The dispatcher's lease check compares (run_id, attempt)

models_disk.description: from API 1.16: the volume holding the models root, measured at every write

root.description: the models root (HELMSTUDIO_MODELS, default ~/GenAI/models) with the home directory written `~`

writable.description: from API 1.18: the runner can write its models root (a container whose models root is bind-mounted read-only reports false: studio refuses its model jobs, 409). Absent = true

machine.description: from API 1.16: what the runner runs on (the Hosts screen's `Apple Silicon · Metal · native`)

hub_token.description: from API 1.16: a Hub token file is present on this host (RUNNER_HF_TOKEN_FILE exists and is not empty); the token itself is never published

policy.description: from API 1.16: the residency settings in effect: the host_settings value of this host, else the runner's env (RUNNER_AFTER_RUN, RUNNER_IDLE_UNLOAD_S / 60, RUNNER_RESERVE_GB, pins RUNNER_PIN)

settings_version.description: the host_settings `version` applied; null = none (env defaults)

media.description: from API 1.17: this env runs media jobs (cmd.media.<host>.<env>: exports and frames; contracts/README.md, Timeline: media jobs). Present only when the runner found ffmpeg >= 6 with the filters xfade, apad, amix and the encoder aac, and at least one H.264 encoder; absent = it runs none

encoders.description: the H.264 encoders it will use, preferred first (h264_videotoolbox, from API 1.18 h264_nvenc: hardware; libx264: software)

thumbs.description: from API 1.48: this env also runs thumbs jobs (contracts/README.md, Thumbnails); absent = an older runner: studio sends it none

loraBlock.description: a family's LoRA rules (the `lora:` block of its model.yaml): what the normaliser needs to apply a LoRA file to this family, and what studio needs to detect a file's family (contracts/README.md, LoRA normaliser). The stack node's row cap, strength range and modes are in the <family>/lora-stack node schema

component.description: the weight component LoRAs patch (transformer); a stage whose `uses` holds it sees the Model's LoRA set

modules.description: the component's Linear module names a LoRA may target (canonical, dotted, as the model's named_modules), sorted; one numeric range `{a..b}` per entry expands to a..b inclusive (transformer_blocks.{0..31}.attn.to_q). The runner generates it from the meta-device model; with every `.` read as `_` the expanded names must still be unique (kohya)

renames.description: family-specific key fixes, in order: the first that matches a key's module part (after the style's prefix and suffix are cut) replaces the matched part with `to`. `at: start` (default): `from` starts the part (a prefix rewrite); `at: end`: `from` ends it (LTX: `.to_out.0` -> `.to_out`). Most families: []

at.description: where `from` must match: start (default) or end of the module part

ignore.description: glob patterns (fnmatch: `*` any run, `?` one character; case-sensitive) over raw tensor keys that are counted as ignored instead of unapplied. Empty = every key must apply

prefused.description: LoRAs already fused into a variant's weights (LTX: the distilled LoRA is part of the distilled transformer): a stack row naming one on a model of that variant is 422 at run (`<node>.<param>[<i>].lora: LoRA <name> is already part of the <variant> weights`), so it is never applied twice. The runner fills lora_id from its LoRA index (model.yaml names the file); absent = none

looks.description: registry key <host>.<env>.looks: the starter looks of this runner's packs (runner_service/packs/<pack>/looks/*.yaml, contracts/README.md Looks: starter looks), written at start (an empty list when its packs ship none). Studio lists the union over live hosts to every user, read-only; a look's id is the same on every host
every look of every pack of this env, by pack, then file name, then file order; ids unique

id.description: <family>/<the YAML id>: the look's id everywhere (LibraryItem.id, RunRequest.looks), stable across hosts

family.description: the pack's family (= the id's first part)

text.description: appended to the prompt; may be empty only when the look has a LoRA

version.description: the YAML version (default 1); a pack bumps it when it changes the look, so reuse can say changed

loras.description: the YAML lora, when it has one

file.description: the file name as written in the YAML, looked up in the folders the LoRA index scans (contracts/README.md, LoRAs: shared)

name.description: the file name without .safetensors, cut to 80 (the index's name)

lora_id.description: the file's SHA-256 = its shared LoRA id in <host>.<env>.loras; null when this host has no such file (studio then takes another live host's)

key.description: packs/<family>/looks/<id>-<first 16 hex of the file's SHA-256>.<ext>: the YAML image, which the runner PUTs to the object store at start unless that key exists (content-addressed, never overwritten). Shown only as the look's thumb_url; never a reference image

studioLayout.description: openapi.yaml StudioLayout (check.py keeps the two equal): which params Create shows and where. Absent = the derived form

keyframes.description: from API 1.37: the image params a Timeline New shot binds a first and a last frame into, for a workflow whose frames are image params rather than keyframe rows (MiniMax H3 Image to video); Workflow.keyframes takes this shape (contracts/README.md, Timeline: New shot options). Not a placement

help.description: from API 1.25: the section's (i) text in Create; absent = no (i)

choices.description: from API 1.26: tiles that lead the section, each a named pick among sets of values (checked as presets); Create shows the option whose set holds

help.description: from API 1.39: the option's line under its name in the tile's menu (LTX's Recipe: Detail)

preset_help.description: from API 1.47: the Preset heading's (i) text: the first item whose `when` holds over the workflow's paths, or that has none

preset_order.description: from API 1.25: every name of presets once, in the order Create shows them (an object's key order is not kept); absent = by name. The runner fills it from the workflow file's key order when the pack leaves it out

custom.description: from API 1.15: registry key `pipelines.engine.custom` (host token `pipelines`, env token `engine`; no hosts key, no nodes): the custom nodes pipelines_service's packs register (contracts/README.md, Custom nodes), written by pipelines at start. studio reads it for the pipeline rules and GET /v1/studio/custom-nodes

input.description: the pydantic input model's JSON schema (model_json_schema(), refs inlined)

output.description: the pydantic output model's JSON schema

network.description: it calls the network: counted as a remote model (off by default, shown at Submit)

version.description: the first 12 hex of the sha256 of the pack's code: Resume asks when it changed

customFields.description: an object JSON schema whose top-level properties are the fields; a field a pipeline may bind is `{type: string}` (text) or `{type: array, items: {type: string, format: uuid}, maxItems ≤ 8}` (take ids); any other field takes only a fixed value

pin.description: one resident entry's identity, as req.runner.unload names it, with its env

compute.description: from API 1.39: the entry's compute; absent = float32

loras.description: a baked set, in order; absent or empty = the plain component

settings.description: from API 1.16: bucket host_settings, key <host>: the admin's residency settings for every env of the host (plan 03-runtime 6.2: one setting per host). studio_service writes it from its own table on every change and at start (its table is the truth; the key is a copy); each runner of the host watches the key and applies a new version at once, between runs (never mid-run), then reports `policy.settings_version` in its hosts key. No key: the runner's env defaults

after_run.description: what stays loaded once a run ends (RUNNER_AFTER_RUN's values): unload = everything, keep_warm = all until memory is needed or idle_unload_min passes, keep_pinned = only the pins

idle_unload_min.description: keep_warm: minutes idle before everything but the pins is unloaded; 0 = never

pins.description: replaces RUNNER_PIN: these entries are marked pinned (pinned_why pin) whenever resident, kept by keep_pinned and the idle unload, a hand-over victim only as the last resort; an admin unload still unloads them

voices.description: registry key <host>.<env>.voices (API 1.30): the starter voices of this runner's packs (runner_service/packs/<pack>/voices/*.yaml, contracts/README.md Voices: starter voices), written at start (an empty list when its packs ship none). Studio lists the union over live hosts to every user as read-only library items of kind voice, group preset; a voice's id is the same on every host
every voice of every pack of this env, by pack, then file name, then file order; ids unique, and none is also a look id of the env

id.description: <family>/<the YAML id>: the voice's id everywhere (LibraryItem.id, a voice param's {voice_id}), stable across hosts

family.description: the pack's family (= the id's first part): the only family whose voice params take it

speaker.description: the model's own speaker id (Qwen3-TTS: Ryan, Uncle_Fu); sent as defs voice `speaker`

language.description: the BCP 47 tag of the voice's own language (en, en-US, zh, pt-BR); the pack maps it to its model's codes

style.description: how it speaks, in words (calm, bright); absent = none

version.description: the YAML version (default 1); a pack bumps it when it changes the voice

key.description: packs/<family>/voices/<id>-<first 16 hex of the file's SHA-256>.wav: the YAML preview clip, which the runner PUTs to the object store at start unless that key exists (content-addressed, never overwritten). Shown only as the voice's thumb_url (a sound tile); never an input

revision.description: a commit SHA (preferred: pinned), tag or branch

allow_patterns.description: fnmatch globs over repo paths; the variant's own components' files and their configs (shared components come from their owner variant's source)

must_accept.description: true: the admin accepts the licence text before the download starts (accept_licence)

gated.description: the repo needs a Hub token: the runner reads it from the host's secrets file (RUNNER_HF_TOKEN_FILE); never in a message, the API or a log

bytes.description: the expected download size of the variant's own files (shown while missing; the job's total_bytes is the hub's)

source.description: where a download fetches files: huggingface_hub.snapshot_download(repo_id=repo, revision=revision, allow_patterns=allow_patterns, local_dir=<models root>/<dir>)

plugin_runs.description: from API 1.67: bucket host_settings, key <host>.plugins: the plugins that are on and declare `run` with that host (contracts/README.md, Plugins: starts itself). studio_service writes it on every change and at start; the host's supervising runner (RUNNER_PLUGINS on) reads it every 5 s and starts or stops each plugin's service to match. Names only: the runner reads each plugin's `run.cmd` from its own plugin folders. No key: none

retry.description: from API 1.67: Try again: a nonce per plugin, raised by turning an on plugin on again; when it changes the runner starts that plugin again at once, its backoff reset

plugins.description: from API 1.67: bucket registry, key <host>.<env>.plugins, written by the host's supervising runner whenever a plugin's state changes: each plugin it was asked to run, by name. starting: launched, not up 3 s yet; running: up; failed: it exited (detail: why, the log's last line) and is started again after the backoff (1 s, doubling to 60 s; reset after 60 s up); stopped: turned off. studio shows Starting…, Running (its health path) and Couldn't start · detail

log.description: the log file, as the host sees it (~/.helm/logs/<plugin>.log)
